015/**
016 * The current state of the outbreak. It contains simulation parameters that
017 * change over simulation time and time varying derived summary data (marked
018 * with 'Lazy' or 'Derived'). Only one state will exist at any one point in a
019 * model and is replaced at each time step.
020 */
021@Value.Immutable
022@SuppressWarnings("immutable")
023public interface OutbreakState extends OutbreakTemporalState {
024
025        // @Value.Default default Double getViralActivityModifier() {return 1.0D;}
026
027        @Override @Value.Lazy
028        default long getAdmissionIncidence() {
029                return ModelNav.peopleState(this)
030                        .filter(p -> !p.isDead())
031                        .filter(PersonState::isIncidentHospitalisation)
032                        .count();
033        }
034

036         * This derived value is the average compliance of the population.

038         * A true value:<br>
039         * <br>
040         *

042         */

044        default double getAverageCompliance() {
045                return ModelNav.peopleState(this)
046                        .mapToDouble(PersonState::getAdjustedCompliance)

099        /**
100         * This derived value is a multinomial count of behaviours of individual
101         * agents in the simulation. This is useful for understanding the
102         * distribution of behaviours in the population. It is a map where the keys
103         * are the behaviour categories and the values are the counts of people in
104         * each category. The behaviour categories are defined by the behaviour model
105         * and can include things like "compliant", "non-compliant", "partially
106         * compliant", etc. The behaviour model is defined by the individual agents
107         * and can change over time based on the state of the outbreak and the
108         * policies in place. This derived value can be used to track how behaviour
109         * changes over time and how it correlates with the course of the outbreak.
110         *
111         * A true value:<br>
112         *
113         * @return A multi-nomial count of behaviours of individual agents in the
114         *         simulation
115         */
116        @Value.Lazy
117        default Map<String, Long> getBehaviourCounts() {
118                return ModelNav.people(this)
119                        .map(Person::getCurrentState)
120                        .collect(
121                                Collectors.groupingByConcurrent(
122                                        PersonState::getBehaviour,
123                                        Collectors.counting()
124                                )
125                        );
126        }
127
128        /**
129         * This derived value is a multinomial count of the number of contacts people
130         * have in the simulation. This is useful for understanding the distribution
131         * of contact patterns in the population. It is a map where the keys are the
132         * number of contacts and the values are the counts of people with that
133         * number of contacts. The contact patterns can be influenced by the
134         * behaviour model, policies in place, and the state of the outbreak. This
135         * derived value can be used to track how contact patterns change over time
136         * and how they correlate with the course of the outbreak.
137         *
138         * A true value:<br>
139         * <br>
140         *
141         * @return A multinomial count of people in the simulation who have had a
142         *         given number of contacts that day.
143         */
144        @Value.Lazy
145        default Map<Long, Long> getContactCounts() {
146                return ModelNav.people(this)
147                        .map(Person::getCurrentState)
148                        .collect(
149                                Collectors.groupingByConcurrent(
150                                        PersonState::getContactCount,
151                                        Collectors.counting()
152                                )
153                        );
154        }
155
156        /**
157         * The contact detected probability is a key parameter for the effectiveness
158         * of contact tracing apps. It represents the technical effectiveness of the
159         * app but not the actual use of the app by individuals.
160         *
161         * A true value:<br>
162         * <br>
163         *
164         * @return A probability that if two people are in contact and both using
165         *         apps then how likely is it that the app will detect the contact?
166         *         The contact detected probability is a system wide parameter and
167         *         describes how technically effective the app is. The individual
168         *         probability of app use, which covers phone actually switched on,
169         *         app installed, and working is captured by
170         *         {@link PersonState#getAdjustedAppUseProbability()}
171         */
172        double getContactDetectedProbability();

219        /**
220         * This derived value is the number of people who are currently hospitalised
221         * at a given point in time versus all the non dead people. This is a key
222         * metric for understanding the burden on the healthcare system and is used
223         * in various places such as to determine healthcare capacity needs and to
224         * inform policy decisions.
225         *
226         * @return Rate of all the people who are needing hospitalisation (excluding
227         *         dead)
228         */

230        default Binomial getHospitalisationRate() {
231                return ModelNav.peopleState(this)
232                        .filter(p -> !p.isDead())
233                        .map(PersonState::isRequiringHospitalisation)
234                        .collect(Binomial.collectBinary());

238         * This derived value is the number of people who are currently hospitalised

240         *

242         * <br>
243         *
244         * @return the number of people who are currently hospitalised at a given
245         *         point in time.
246         */
247        @Override @Value.Lazy
248        default long getHospitalisedCount() {
249                return this.getHospitalisationRate()
250                        .getNumerator();
251        }

324        /**
325         * The estimate of the incubation period is important as it puts a time on
326         * how long to isolate and when to test after exposure.
327         *
328         * @return an estimate of the incubation period in days.
329         */
330        int getPresumedIncubationPeriod();

332        /**
333         * The current best estimate of how long an infectious person is infectious
334         * for.
335         *
336         * The estimate of the infectious period is important because it informs the
337         * policy and behavioural guidance on a whole range of things, from self
338         * isolation duration to maximum time that an infectious contact is deemed
339         * relevant. A grossly mis-specified value could lead to a decrease in
340         * effectiveness of behavioural interventions. Assumptions around this define
341         * how long policy models suggest self isolation.
342         *
343         * @return an estimate of the infectious period in days.
344         */
345        int getPresumedInfectiousPeriod();
346
347        /**
348         * An estimate of how sensitive symptoms are is part of determining their
349         * significance if they are being recorded by an smart agent.
350         *
351         * @return an estimate of the symptom sensitivity as a probability.
352         */
353        double getPresumedSymptomSensitivity();
354
355        /**
356         * An estimate of how specific symptoms are is part of determining their
357         * significance if they are being recorded by an smart agent.

359         * @return an estimate of the symptom specificity as a probability.

361        double getPresumedSymptomSpecificity();

363        /**
364         * This derived value is the number of people who have had at least one
365         * positive test over the last infectious period versus all the non dead
366         * people who have had at least one test result. This is one of the key
367         * determinants of the {@link io.github.ai4ci.abm.policy.PolicyModel}
368         * lockdown decision making, but is heavily biased by symptomatic testing.
369         *
370         * @return All the people who tested positive over the last infectious period
371         *         versus all the non dead people. This is one of the key
372         *         determinants of the {@link io.github.ai4ci.abm.policy.PolicyModel}
373         *         lockdown decision making, but may be somewhat biased by
374         *         symptomatic testing
375         */
376        @Value.Lazy
377        default Binomial getPresumedTestPositivePrevalence() {
378                return this.getPresumedTestPositivity(t -> true, false);
379                // return ((double) pos) /
380                // (this.getEntity().getSetupConfiguration().getNetworkSize() -
381                // this.getCumulativeDeaths());
382        }
383
384        /**
385         * This derived value is the number of people who have had at least one
386         * positive test over the last infectious period versus all the people who
387         * have had at least one test result. This is one of the key determinants of
388         * the {@link io.github.ai4ci.abm.policy.PolicyModel} lockdown decision
389         * making, but is heavily biased by symptomatic testing.
390         *
391         * @return All the people who had at least one positive test over the last
392         *         infectious period versus those that has tests that were all
393         *         negative. This is one of the key determinants of the
394         *         {@link io.github.ai4ci.abm.policy.PolicyModel} lockdown decision
395         *         making, but is heavily biased by symptomatic testing
396         */
397        @Value.Lazy
398        default Binomial getPresumedTestPositivity() {
399                return this.getPresumedTestPositivity(t -> true, true);
400        }
401
402        /**
403         * Count of people with at least one positive vs either all non dead or all
404         * people who have a test result.
405         *
406         * @param filter    a predicate to select the type of test to look at (e.g.
407         *                  by indication or by test type)
408         * @param wasTested should the denominator include only people with tests
409         *                  done, or everyone?
410         * @return All the people who had at least one positive test over the last
411         *         infectious period versus either all the non dead people or all the
412         *         people who have had at least one test result. This is one of the
413         *         key determinants of the
414         *         {@link io.github.ai4ci.abm.policy.PolicyModel} lockdown decision
415         *         making, but is heavily biased by symptomatic testing
416         *
417         */
418        default Binomial getPresumedTestPositivity(
419                        Predicate<TestResult> filter, boolean wasTested
420        ) {
421                return ModelNav.peopleState(this)
422                        .filter(p -> !p.isDead())
423                        .map(
424                                p -> p.getStillRelevantTests()
425                                        .filter(tr -> tr.isResultAvailable(this.getTime()))
426                                        .filter(filter)
427                                        .map(TestResult::getFinalObservedResult)
428                                        .collect(Binomial.collectBinary())
429                                // result of this is the Binomial of tests for an individual
430                        )
431                        .filter(
432                                // exclude people that have had no tests
433                                b -> wasTested ? b.getDenominator() != 0 : true
434                        )
435                        .map(
436                                // any positive results will be collected in the numerator
437                                // This is true = any positive tests; false = no positive
438                                // tests
439                                b -> b.getNumerator() > 0
440                        )
441                        .collect(Binomial.collectBinary());
442        }
443
444        @Override @Value.Lazy
445        default double getPrevalence() {
446                return ((double) this.getInfectedCount()) / (this.getEntity()
447                        .getPopulationSize() - this.getCumulativeDeaths());
448        }
449
450        /**
451         * This derived value is an estimate of the R_t value based on the renewal
452         * equation. This is not using a realised infection network as in the present
453         * model there are exposures but it is not explicit which exposure is
454         * actually responsible for infection. It is based on the number of people
455         * who are newly exposed today (the numerator) and the number of people with
456         * capability to infect today (the denominator). The denominator is
457         * calculated using the infectivity profile from the baseline configuration
458         * and the history of incidence.
459         *
460         * @return An estimate of the R_t value based on the renewal equation. This
461         *         is not using a realised infection network as in the present model
462         *         there are exposures but it is not explicit which exposure is
463         *         actually responsible for infection.
464         */
465        default double getRtEffective() {
466                // people who are newly exposed today
467                var numerator = this.getIncidence();
468                // people with capability to infect today. (n.b. those infected today will
469                // have zero capability)
470                var dd = this.getEntity()
471                        .getBaseline()
472                        .getInfectivityProfile();
473
474                var denominator = IntStream.range(0, (int) dd.size())
475                        .mapToDouble(
476                                tau -> this.getEntity()
477                                        .getHistory(tau)
478                                        .map(OutbreakHistory::getIncidence)
479                                        .orElse(0L) * dd.condDensity(tau)
480                        )
481                        .sum();
482
483                return denominator == 0 ? Double.NaN : (numerator) / denominator;
484        }

486        /**
487         * The screening probability is the probability that any randomly selected
488         * person in the model will get a screening test performed today. This
489         * represents mass screening or asymptomatic testing programmes which inform
490         * policy decisions and can give less biased estimates of prevalence than
491         * symptomatic testing.
492         *
493         * A true value:<br>
494         * <br>
495         *
496         * @return A probability that any randomly selected person in the model will
497         *         get a screening test performed today.
498         */
499        double getScreeningProbability();
500
501        /**
502         * This derived value is the number of people who have had at least one
503         * positive test over the last infectious period versus all the people who
504         * have had at least one test result for screening tests only. This is one of
505         * the key determinants of the {@link io.github.ai4ci.abm.policy.PolicyModel}
506         * lockdown decision making, but is less biased by symptomatic testing as it
507         * only includes screening tests.
508         *
509         * @return All the people who had at least one positive test over the last
510         *         infectious period versus those that has tests that were all
511         *         negative. This is one of the key determinants of the
512         *         {@link io.github.ai4ci.abm.policy.PolicyModel} lockdown decision
513         *         making, and excludes reactive / symptomatic testing so is in
514         *         theory unbiased.
515         */
516        @Value.Lazy
517        default Binomial getScreeningTestPositivity() {
518                return this.getPresumedTestPositivity(
519                        t -> t.getIndication()
520                                .equals(Indication.SCREENING),
521                        true
522                );
523        }

525        /**
526         * This derived value is the number of people experiencing symptoms at a
527         * given point in time.
528         *
529         * <p>
530         * A true value
531         *
532         * @return the number of people experiencing symptoms at a given point in
533         *         time

535        @Value.Lazy
536        default long getSymptomaticCount() {
537                return ModelNav.peopleState(this)

540                        .count();
541        }

543        /**
544         * This derived value is the number of people with test negatives in the
545         * results that become available
546         *
547         * A true but also observed value (assuming no additional reporting delay).
548         * This does not account for the nature of the test.
549         *
550         * @return count of people with test negatives in the results that become
551         *         available today. (Does not count people with no test results
552         *         today). The number of tests reported negative on the current
553         *         simulation date. This is reported on the date the test result is
554         *         available (not when the test was taken). N.B. largely only used
555         *         for reporting now
556         */
557        @Value.Lazy
558        default long getTestNegativesByResultDate() {
559                return ModelNav.peopleCurrentHistory(this)
560                        .mapToInt(p -> {// If any of a
561                                                                        // persons
562                                                                        // results are
563                                                                        // positive
564                                                                        // today
565                                if (p.getTodaysResults()
566                                        .isEmpty()) return 0;
567                                return p.getTodaysResults()
568                                        .stream()
569                                        .map(TestResult::getFinalResult)
570                                        .allMatch(tr -> tr.equals(Result.NEGATIVE)) ? 1 : 0;
571                        })
572                        .sum();
573        }
574
575        /**
576         * This derived value is the number of people with test positives in the
577         * results that become available
578         *
579         * A true but also observed value (assuming no additional reporting delay).
580         * This does not account for the nature of the test.
581         *
582         * @return Count of people with test positives in the results that become
583         *         available today.The number of tests reported positive on the
584         *         current simulation date. This is reported on the date the test
585         *         result is available (not when the test was taken). N.B. largely
586         *         only used for reporting now
587         */
588        @Value.Lazy
589        default long getTestPositivesByResultDate() {
590                return ModelNav.peopleCurrentHistory(this)
591                        .mapToInt(p ->
592                        // If any of a persons results are positive today
593                        p.getTodaysResults()
594                                .stream()
595                                .map(TestResult::getFinalResult)
596                                .anyMatch(tr -> tr.equals(Result.POSITIVE)) ? 1 : 0
597                        )
598                        .sum();
599        }

601        @Override @Value.Lazy
602        default long getTimeToMaximumIncidence() {
603                if (this.getIncidence() > ModelNav.history(this)
604                        .map(OutbreakHistory::getMaximumIncidence)
605                        .orElse(0L)) return this.getTime();
606                return ModelNav.history(this)
607                        .map(OutbreakHistory::getTimeToMaximumIncidence)
608                        .orElse(0L);
609        }

631         * Average absolute loss of mobility compared to baseline.

633         * A true value:<br>

651        /**
652         * The transmissibility modifier is a catch all parameter that can be used to
653         * capture changes in transmission that are not captured by the other
654         * parameters such as mobility, compliance, contact detection probability or
655         * viral load. It is intended to capture things like weather effects, or
656         * viral evolution that may change the transmissibility of the virus over
657         * time.
658         *
659         * A true value:<br>
660         * <br>
661         *
662         * @return An odds ratio describing day to day changes in the transmission
663         *         due to exogenous factors such as weather, or potentially viral
664         *         evolution. None of these are yet defined but {@link ModelUpdate}
665         *         will be where they are implemented and configured as a function of
666         *         time similar to the way
667         *         {@link io.github.ai4ci.config.execution.DemographicAdjustment} are
668         *         handled (although that has an additional override that I don't
669         *         think we will need here).
670         */
671        double getTransmissibilityModifier();
672
673        /**
674         * The value or statistic that is used to trigger lockdowns. There are
675         * various metrics that could trigger a policy change such as absolute case
676         * count, or test positivity rate
677         *
678         * @see io.github.ai4ci.abm.policy.Trigger.Value
679         *
680         * @return the value or statistic that is used to trigger lockdowns

682        Trigger.Value getTriggerValue();
